ideas.title: Low tide: the sea goes out and leaves a sailing flat
ideas.critique: A coastline that really moves twice a day is something the island has never done, and it puts a clock and a risk into sailing. As pitched, though, the tide is a sine on the sea level over a reshaped beach, and wet versus dry sand is a lookup by height. That is a rig, not a sea, and the race back only works if the flood actually catches the cart.

ideas.title: Trim by ear: the sail's own sound
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Hearing the solved flow, with real shedding and stall noise from the box, is a fresh sense for the island, and steering by ear is a real skill. Its weak points: the synth that maps forces to sound is hand-tuned, and it gives feedback for a sailing control the player does not have yet.

ideas.title: Kite buggy: a kite pulls the cart
ideas.critique: Diving a two-line kite through its wind window is the most playable thing on the list, and the surges come from a real solver and real ropes. But it goes off to the side of the road rather than along it: one more wind toy next to a yacht that is not sailable yet.

ideas.title: Push-start: Lumi and a friend shove the yacht
ideas.critique: It hits the big goal's moment, where the friends push, and traction limited by the sand is the right law. As a thing to watch it is a pose plus a force added to a balance, and the claim that two pushers beat 69 N is a number written in.

ideas.title: Lumi's helmsman pose: beak on the tiller, hanging out
ideas.critique: Heel that can really lift a wheel and tip the cart, with Lumi's body as the counterweight, makes the yacht a thing you sail and Lumi a character you recognise. The risk is a canned lean animation laid over a heel angle, with the body not actually moving the mass.

ideas.title: Tracks in the wet sand that the tide erases
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A day's sailing written on the beach is a lovely picture, but it is mostly something to look at, and it needs both the tide and the sailing to exist first. Ruts stamped into a height field and then smoothed by a decay rule is the plainest version of it.

ideas.title: A storm night: the sail rips and Lumi sews it
ideas.critique: A membrane loaded by the solved pressure field that tears where it is weakest is real new physics, and a repair that changes the sail is a good loop. Its payoff, though, is the island's familiar 'load it until it fails' beat again, and the sewing is likely to end up a click.

ideas.title: The friends' tide-pool fishing from the yacht
ideas.critique: It moves a behaviour the island already has to a new place, and it rests entirely on two systems that do not exist yet: the tide and friends who ride. Stranded fish 'in the water mask' read as markers, not bodies.

ideas.title: Wind map from the dune grass
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Sand blowing off the crests above a real threshold, driven by the solved field, is honest new particle physics. But bending grass and cat's-paws are what anyone expects of a wind, and reading the wind only matters once there is something to sail.

ideas.title: Beached: the yacht gets stuck in soft sand
ideas.critique: This is the big goal's own plank-versus-sand law turned into a problem the player solves, with sinkage that grows with slip in the sand field. It can only be as good as that coupling: if the burying is a scripted stuck state, it is just a wall.
